title: Prime-ray order consumers, finite-support escape, and unbounded prime-divisor supply

concepts.label: bounded-degree exact-order consumer
concepts.note: Every prime divisor of a layer C(mq) supplies a witness k between 1 and d with mq dividing p^k-1.

concepts.label: eventual escape from finite prime support
concepts.note: Every prescribed finite set of rational primes is absent from sufficiently remote prime-ray layers.

concepts.label: eventual nontrivial clean layer supply
concepts.note: At sufficiently large prime indices, C(mq) is nontrivial and coprime to mq.

concepts.label: unbounded prime divisors on remote prime indices
concepts.note: Beyond arbitrary size and index thresholds, a layer C(mq) has a prime divisor larger than the size threshold.

concepts.label: abstract producer boundary
concepts.note: The generic theorems transport order and layer-supply hypotheses; they do not establish those hypotheses for an arbitrary layer or prove a carry kill or irrationality.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: Let m>0. If every prime divisor p of every prime-index layer C(mq) has some exact-order witness exponent k with 1≤k≤d and mq dividing p^k-1, then for every finite set S of primes there is a threshold Q₀ such that no p in S divides C(mq) whenever q is prime and q≥Q₀.
open_antecedents: Instantiate BoundedDegreeOrderConsumer C m d for the layer family of interest; positivity of m is the theorem's explicit arithmetic side condition.
statement_nodes.engine: For a finite support S, choose the index threshold above ∑_{p∈S} p^d. If p∈S divided a later layer, the order consumer would give mq≤p^k-1<q, contradicting q≤mq when m>0.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: This is the standard finiteness consequence of a uniform degree bound on multiplicative-order witnesses, packaged for the repository's prime-ray layer interface.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: No nontrivial-layer or Archimedean growth hypothesis is needed for this exclusion step. Conversely, exclusion alone does not show that any layer has a prime divisor, produce a large divisor, prove a carry discrepancy, or imply irrationality.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: If C has eventual nontrivial clean layers on the prime ray mq and those layers eventually escape every prescribed finite prime support, then for every size bound B and prime-index lower bound N₀ there are primes q≥N₀ and p>B such that p divides C(mq).
open_antecedents: Instantiate PrimeRayLayerSupply C m, supplying eventual nontriviality of C(mq).
Instantiate FinitePrimeSupportEscape C m for the same layer family.
statement_nodes.engine: Apply finite-support escape to all naturals below B+1, choose a prime q above the supply, escape, and requested index thresholds, take a prime divisor of the nontrivial layer, and exclude that divisor from the bounded range.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: The passage from eventual nontriviality plus escape from each finite support to unbounded prime divisors is an elementary compact finite-support argument.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: The theorem consumes, rather than proves, both layer supply and finite-support escape. It is existential and supplies no effective least q or p; the coprimality component of PrimeRayLayerSupply is stronger than what this proof uses. No target avoidance, carry kill, or irrationality follows.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: Let m>0. If C has eventual nontrivial clean layers on the prime ray mq and every prime divisor of C(mq) has an exact-order witness in some degree k≤d, then the prime divisors of those layers are unbounded even after imposing an arbitrary lower bound on the prime index q.
open_antecedents: Instantiate PrimeRayLayerSupply C m for the layer family of interest.
Instantiate BoundedDegreeOrderConsumer C m d for a uniform finite degree d; positivity of m is explicit.
statement_nodes.engine: Compose bounded-degree order realisability with finite-support escape, then compose that escape theorem with eventual nontrivial layer supply.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: The result is a direct composition of the two exact generic interfaces. The X-2/Mersenne specialization is discharged unconditionally elsewhere; this node makes no broader polynomial-realisability claim.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: For the concrete X-2 layer, Z35 records unconditional supply and degree-one order hypotheses. For arbitrary layers, polynomial/resultant order realisability and Archimedean nontriviality remain inputs. Even unbounded prime support supplies only arithmetic anchors, not cofinal certified kills or irrationality of the binary totient series.

declaration_roles.routing_basis: The paper-selected theorem is exact direct evidence for the first producer stage: bounded-degree order witnesses imply finite-support escape without a layer-supply assumption.
This exact source theorem is the unlisted middle bridge needed to interpret the full structural family and the composition used by the paper-selected endpoint.
The paper-selected endpoint composes the two generic stages and is instantiated unconditionally for the X-2 layer in CyclotomicAnchoredKill.

intra_zone_relations.basis: The complete producer first applies finitePrimeSupportEscape_of_orderConsumer to the bounded-degree order hypothesis.
The complete producer then supplies the derived finite-support escape and the assumed layer supply to the generic unbounded-prime-divisor bridge.
The first theorem produces the finite-support escape interface from order witnesses; the second consumes that interface together with nontrivial layer supply.
